insider_note: Three points separate them: what moves, which way, and whether a membrane is needed. The membrane is the one examiners look for.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Osmosis
steps.margin_note: What moves, which way, and the membrane. Four lines.
lines: Osmosis is the movement of SOLVENT (water)
molecules from a lower concentrated solution
steps.why: Osmosis is defined by the solvent moving toward the stronger solution, which is only possible when a membrane holds the solute back.
common_mistakes: Saying the solute moves. In osmosis the SOLVENT (water) moves.
Leaving out the membrane. Osmosis cannot happen without a semipermeable membrane.
steps.memory_tip: Osmosis moves water toward the stronger side, and only through a membrane.

steps.label: Diffusion
steps.margin_note: Mirror the osmosis lines point for point. The contrast is the mark.

lines.text: Osmosis needs a membrane; diffusion does not

lines: Diffusion is the movement of SOLUTE molecules
from a higher concentrated solution to a lower
It need NOT require a membrane.
steps.why: Diffusion runs the opposite way with the opposite particle and needs no barrier, so every part of the osmosis line is reversed here.
common_mistakes: Writing that diffusion also needs a membrane. It does not.
Giving the same direction for both. Osmosis is low to high solution; diffusion is high to low.
steps.memory_tip: Water to the strong side with a membrane; solute to the weak side without one.
